fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear vehicle passage from the street to the parking area.
• Cut back dense plantings near the front entry to keep the main entry path visible and unobstructed for approaching responders.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing at the rear of the property unlocked to allow responders to reach the rear yard without circling back to the front.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through vegetation.
• Post the property address visibly at the street frontage so responders can confirm the correct property on approach.
• Keep the parking area clear of stored vehicles or equipment that would block responder staging near the front of the house.
• Thin dense plantings along the perimeter fencing so responders can see the fence line and locate access points quickly.
• Mark any secondary access points in the fencing with a visible indicator so responders can find them without a full perimeter walk.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to reduce the amount of combustible material close to the building.
• Separate individual scattered trees from each other and from the structure by removing lower branches and any shrubs growing between them.
• Trim or remove vegetation that is growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath tree clusters clear of dead leaves, needles, and fallen branches.
• Remove any shrubs or small plants growing at the base of trees nearest to the structure.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by keeping them free of debris, dead plant material, and new plant growth.
